body:
Essentially in the README for each plugin, at the bottom, a list of plugins serving a similar purpose is outlined. Are the libraries provided by mini.nvim replacements for those?

For example, the fuzzy finder has a "similar plugin" telescope.nvim. Telescope is something I use frequently, would the provided fuzzy finder in mini achieve much of the same capabilities as telescope?

What about mini snippets compared to something like nvim-cmp?

Thanks.

comment_data.body:
For most of them the answer is "yes, to a degree, if not explicitly said otherwise". There are more details in the help files:
- ['mini.pick'](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/14ce72476995255fc5cb919da8067f65865e1225/doc/mini-pick.txt#L99-L114) comparisons. I would say it is on par with 'telescope.nvim' *if* 'mini.extra' is also set up.
- 'mini.snippets' is a snippets engine and loader. Its comparisons are [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/14ce72476995255fc5cb919da8067f65865e1225/doc/mini-snippets.txt#L84-L120). 'nvim-cmp' is an autocompletion engine and its 'mini.nvim' alternative is 'mini.completion'. Here are [its comparisons to similar plugins](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/14ce72476995255fc5cb919da8067f65865e1225/doc/mini-completion.txt#L151-L164).
